newsitem.title: USA: U.S. budget negotiators say had good first meeting.
newsitem.headline: U.S. budget negotiators say had good first meeting.

text.p: Congressional and White House negotiators said Tuesday's initial budget negotiation was a good first session and hoped progress towards a balanced budget would be made this week.

Senate Budget Committee chairman Pete Domenici, Republican of New Mexico, called the session, "a solid meeting...a very successful 3-1/2 hours of discussion." The session centered on the administration's proposed changes in the Medicare program.

Office of Management and Budget Director Frank Raines said the administration will stand by its commitment to $100 billion of savings in the program. The Congressional Budget Office said the White House plan would save only $81.6 billion over the five years from this program.
"We are pleased that we are making progress as the president asked all of us to make progress... We hope as our discussions move forward we will be able to find that common ground," said Raines.

Democratic Rep. John Spratt of South Carolina, his party's senior member on the House Budget Committee, called the talks "useful" and cautioned against drawing conclusions from this session. "We are a long, long way off. We shouldn't raise false expectations today. What we are doing right now essentially is talking to each other."

Health and Human Services Secretary Donna Shalala, the head of the National Economic Council, Gene Sperling, and White House congressional liason John Hilley were the senior administration representatives in the meeting. House Budget Committee chairman John Kasich, Republican of Ohio and Sen. Frank Lautenberg of New Jersey, the senior Democrat on the Senate Budget Committee, also attended the meeting.
